title: “Double Threat” to Private Communications: Undemocratic Chat Control Backroom Deals and Imminent Concessions Spark Relaunch of fightchatcontrol.eu
body: This was a Patrick Breyer mobilization alert dated 28 June 2026, warning of a “double attack” on encrypted messaging ahead of an “imminent” Friday-and-Monday EU weekend (Council on 28 June, a feared “final” Chat Control 2.0 trilogue on 29 June). We picked it up on 22 July — about three and a half weeks after that weekend came and went. The kicker: the concessions it warned about never landed. The 29 June trilogue produced no deal, negotiators couldn't agree to make suspicionless scanning permanent, and talks slipped to September. Running an urgent warning about a weekend that already passed — with the opposite outcome to the one predicted — would be less journalism than bad time travel. The underlying fight is real and we've covered it straight (see “Parliament Voted Against Chat Control. It Passed Anyway.” on the 9 July derogation vote, and “The Version That Actually Matters” on the 29 June trilogue), so this expired pre-event alert goes in the bin rather than onto the front page.
rejection_reason: Stale advocacy procedural drift + inverted outcome | Breyer pre-event alert for the 28-29 Jun weekend; trilogue produced no deal, live angle already published (chat-control-1-0-survives-parliament-9-jul-vote).
